His comments came as the US Treasury Department imposed new Iran-related sanctions on eight entities based in Canada, according to a notice on its website.
In a separate move on Friday, the Treasury blocked US banks from dealing with MEXC Global, a cryptocurrency exchange registered in the Seychelles.
It accused the exchange of handling at least $16bn in illegal transactions linked to Iran, North Korea and Russia, helping them get around sanctions.
On Thursday, the Treasury sanctioned companies and individuals in India and Turkey that it accused of helping Iran evade restrictions on its oil exports and airlines.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the same day that Washington would continue to pursue anyone supporting Tehran.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Attacks, raids and forced demolitions mark another day of Israeli violence in West Bank
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Attacks, raids and forced demolitions mark another day of Israeli violence in West Bank
Israeli forces and settlers carried out 20 attacks on Palestinian olive pickers in six West Bank governorates on Friday, according to the Palestinian Wall and Colonization Resistance Commission.
The attacks included detentions, assaults, uprooting of trees and theft of crops, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported, citing the commission. Farmers were also blocked from their fields.
West of Jericho, Israeli settlers entered farmland in ad-Duyuk at-Tahta with their sheep. They destroyed crops and greenhouses, resident Mustafa Fheidat told Wafa.
He estimated the damage at hundreds of thousands of shekels.
East of Ramallah, Israeli forces raided the Abu Fazaa Bedouin community for more than three hours, smashing vehicles, assaulting residents and detaining one man.
In Hebron, Israeli forces closed several Old City neighbourhoods for Jewish holidays, including the Ibrahimi Mosque, which will stay closed to Muslims until Saturday night.
Forces also detained three Palestinians, including a journalist, in Hebron and Masafer Yatta, assaulting a fourth.
Among them was Mohammad Yousef Makhmareh, a man with a disability, who was detained in Khirbet al-Markaz after soldiers tried to take his sheep. He lost a hand years ago to a landmine left by Israeli forces.
In occupied East Jerusalem, two Palestinians were forced to demolish their own homes, which housed 18 people, in Jabal al-Mukabber.
The families had paid 25,000 shekels trying to prevent the demolitions.
Palestinians from the village of Abu Falah, accompanied by activists, try to harvest their olives while Israeli forces declare the area a closed military zone, 6 November 2026 (Jess Flom/Reuters)

data.title: Middle East Eye: Cair shuts down Florida office as judge declines reversal of terrorist designation
data.author: MEE staff

Governor Ron DeSantis has made the Muslim civil liberties group a key target alongside foreign political entities and drug cartels
The logo of the Council on American Islamic Relations' office in Florida is shown in an undated photo (Facebook/Cair)
Off
The Council on American Islamic Relations (Cair) has shut down its operations in Florida after a judge declined to reverse the terrorist designation of the group that the state legislature and the governor had imposed earlier this year.
Chief Judge Allen C Winsor of the US District Court for the Northern District of Florida made his decision on Wednesday, while acknowledging Florida's “novel - and perhaps unprecedented" new law allowing for terrorist designations of non-profit groups without due process.
But ultimately, he said Cair's emergency request did not adequately prove that the group was suffering a criminal punishment.
Winsor did, however, say Florida officials cannot prevent Cair from accessing legal services. Florida officials also pledged not to prosecute Cair's board, its staff, or its third-party associates.
Cair has said it will now appeal the decision.
A visit to the website CairFlorida.org on Friday only produced the following message on a dark backdrop: "We have suspended our operations in Florida because of Governor [Ron] DeSantis and other state officials’ baseless and unconstitutional enforcement of the state’s unprecedented new 'domestic terrorist organization' laws against us. The ACLU, SPLC, and their partners are representing us in a federal lawsuit challenging this designation on First Amendment and due process grounds."
In a statement, the Florida Department of Law Enforcement called Winsor's ruling "the right call for the safety of Floridians" and said it "remains vigilant against threats and committed to keeping Floridians safe".

data.title: Middle East Eye: Yemen's Houthis granting ships safe passage via email: Report
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Yemen's Houthis granting ships safe passage via email: Report
Yemen’s Houthis are controlling maritime transit of the Red Sea through a system under which vessels can request safe passage via email, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
The Houthis, who control swaths of Yemen, declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia earlier this year, after which some ships began contacting them before transiting the Red Sea, the Journal reported.
If the Houthis reply, they typically do so within 24 hours, the newspaper said, citing crew member accounts and emails it reviewed.
The Journal included one email in which the master of an unnamed ship declared it “has no connections with Israel, the United Kingdom and the United States of America” and said “we kindly request your confirmation for safe passage.”
Vessels allegedly linked to those countries have been repeatedly targeted by the Houthis.
In another email, the Houthis responded to a separate request from a Chinese container ship: “We hope you are keeping well. We are glad that you understood the criteria for the scope of the vessels ban,” they said.
The Houthis said the ship had a permit for transit that is valid for seven days, adding: “We also invite you to subscribe to our email alert service to receive the latest news and updates.”

data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Iran's health ministry denies report on iodine distribution over US strike fears
Iran's health ministry has denied a report by The Times of London that it was distributing iodine tablets near its nuclear sites to prepare for possible US strikes.
"No Ministry of Health official has spoken to The Times, and the quote attributed to the ministry is false," Hossein Kermanpour, head of the ministry's public relations and information centre, wrote on X.
He said the health system was prepared for various scenarios and threats from "an enemy that does not even spare children". But he added that declaring a state of war was not within the ministry's authority.
He called publishing unverified reports at such a time "irresponsible".
The Times of London had cited an unnamed health ministry official who said Iran was handing out iodine tablets to communities near its nuclear facilities.
The official was quoted as saying, “Trump can no longer be trusted. He may go through with this crime," and that in every war, Iran had tried to distribute the tablets, which help protect the thyroid gland from radiation, within two to three kilometres of its nuclear sites.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Macklemore says US venues rejected his Free Palestine tour
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Macklemore says US venues rejected his Free Palestine tour
American rapper Macklemore said on Friday that major US concert venues, including New York's Madison Square Garden, refused to book his Free Palestine tour that just concluded three dates in Europe.
The rapper launched the effort after he was removed as the opening act on musician Ed Sheeran's concert tour in August, because the stadium owners had objected to him saying "Free Palestine" on stage.
Since then, nine US venues declined to allow him to book available dates through the end of the year, Macklemore said on social media. The venues included Madison Square Garden and the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.
"The shows were not going to be allowed to happen in these venues," he said in a post. "In over 20 years of touring, I've never experienced anything like this."
Macklemore played Free Palestine shows in Dublin, Paris and London to raise funds for organisations that support Palestinians. The musician said he would work with other artists and organisers to do more performances for the cause.
"We live in a country that prides itself on freedom of speech," he wrote. "Yet we've reached a point where a handful of billionaires can decide which causes are acceptable, which voices are welcome and which human lives are worth defending."

data.author: Hilal Saki

Harmeet Dhillon, who led anti-Israel campus protest crackdown, resigns
Several senior US Justice Department officials have resigned, including Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon who was one of the department’s leads in the administration’s efforts to crack down against anti-Israel protests on college campuses.
US Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Trump, announced on Thursday that he had accepted the resignation of Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon.
According to Democracy Now, Dhillon spent her 19-month tenure "gutting" civil rights, and diversity, equity and inclusion protections in education, and led the campaign to target dozens of universities nationwide over student-led pro-Palestine activism and campus protests.
It added that under Dhillon, the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division stopped investigating accusations of systemic racism and sexism.
Dhillon was also directly involved in unsuccessful attempts to obtain voter registration lists from some 30 states ahead of this week's midterm elections that dealt heavy defeats to Trump's Republican Party.
In her resignation letter, cited by US media outlets, Dillon said that she submitted it in October and agreed to remain in her position until the election.
Blanche also announced on Friday the resignations of Assistant Attorney General for National Security John Eisenberg, and Jason Reding Quinones, US attorney for the Southern District of Florida.
Quinones oversaw an investigation into former intelligence officials whom Trump accused of seeking to remove him from power.
The Justice Department under Trump has pursued cases against a number of perceived enemies, and several prosecutors have lost their jobs over their reluctance or inability to bring charges.

data.title: Middle East Eye: UKMTO says 11 ships attacked in week to 4 Nov in Hormuz, Arabian Gulf
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
UKMTO says 11 ships attacked in week to 4 Nov in Hormuz, Arabian Gulf
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has reported 11 attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Arabian Gulf in the seven days to November 4, including incidents that left three vessels sunk.
Eight attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and three in the Arabian Gulf, according to UKMTO's weekly overview. Of the 11 incidents, three vessels continued their voyages, five required assistance and three sank.
The report said one dhow was struck by an unidentified projectile on 2 November, killing one crew member, while 13 others were rescued by local authorities.
A Panama-flagged supply vessel was also struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 November and reportedly sank after a nearby merchant vessel rescued its crew.
A Marshall Islands-flagged tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles in the Arabian Gulf on 4 November, leaving it drifting and requiring assistance from local authorities.
Combined Strait of Hormuz traffic reached 325 transits in the seven-day reporting period, comprising 170 outbound and 155 inbound movements, compared with 277 in the previous week. UKMTO said traffic remained approximately 65 percent below pre-conflict levels.
Automatic Identification System-observed transits increased to 71 from 64 the previous week, while US-reported facilitated transits remained broadly stable. Around 80 percent of Strait of Hormuz transits continued to involve energy carriers.
UKMTO also reported an increase in vessels using the southern route, although most ships broadcasting AIS continued to use the Iranian route.
In the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, no attacks on shipping were reported during the week. The last reported attack was on August 24, 65 days earlier. However, Bab el-Mandeb transits remained 24 percent below levels recorded before the Houthi blockade announcement on July 22.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US offers $20 million reward for info on Iran's nuclear programme
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US offers $20 million reward for info on Iran's nuclear programme
Washington is offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war.
A State Department programme, Rewards for Justice, "is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," US Central Command said on X.
The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.
In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations" has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.
It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward.

'Crisis cannot be left unresolved': Qatar PM says mediation efforts continue
Qatar’s Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, has said that efforts at mediation between Iran and the United States remain active to prevent escalation, warning that the crisis "cannot be left unresolved".
During a public interview at Oxford University on Friday, Al Thani said that “for the past couple of weeks, we have worked with colleagues in the US administration who have very genuine intentions to find a way to contain the situation and de-escalate it".
He said that mediation efforts continue “to prevent the situation from spiralling out of control,” adding that “thanks also to some wise voices in Tehran, we have prevented that from getting out of control.”
He said that even after the US midterm election, the "intentions are still there, the willingness to take steps toward finding a solution is still there and we are building and capitalising on this".
The Prime Minister stressed that "our engagement did not stop and will not stop", although the current pace of diplomatic exchanges may not "be as active as it was a few days ago”.
Qatar earlier dismissed reports claiming negotiations between the US and Iran have failed, warning that such claims benefit “only those seeking to prolong the war”.
Al Thani said mediation efforts continue to prevent a major escalation. (AFP)

data.title: Middle East Eye: US urges citizens across Middle East to exercise 'heightened caution'
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US urges citizens across Middle East to exercise 'heightened caution'
The United States has urged Americans currently in the Middle East to exercise "heightened vigilance" due to the "increased threat of armed attacks by Houthis and Iranian efforts to target US government officials in the region".
"Be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions," reads an alert issued by the Department of State on X.
The Department of State and multiple US embassies/missions across the MiddleEast issued security alerts for Israel, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Qatar, Oman, Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, UAE and Lebanon.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump says US knocked out Iranian 'little bit of anti-aircraft device'
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Trump says US knocked out Iranian 'little bit of anti-aircraft device'
US President Donald Trump says Washington had made considerable progress in its dealings with Iran, while acknowledging that US forces had carried out limited strikes against targets on the country.
"I don't want to talk about it. We do minor strikes. But they knocked out... and they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device. And we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five," Trump told reporters when asked about reports of strikes near Iran's Qeshm Island.
Speaking to reporters after arriving aboard Air Force One at Donald J. Trump International Airport, Trump said the United States was taking out more Iranian oil than before the conflict.
"We've made a lot of progress with Iran, we're taking out more oil now than we were before the war. It's not a war," he said.
"You know, in Russia-Ukraine, they lose 25,000 people a month. We haven't lost anybody in seven months, so I don't think that's a war. Total control. But we're dealing with the Iranians, we'll see how that all works out."
Report by Reuters

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says
Iran's military is "stronger" and more motivated than it was when the United States and Israel started the war in February, says Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia.
"Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," Akraminia said, according to the state news agency Irna.
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
Akraminia said that Iranian armed forces retained control over the Strait of Hormuz and that it would remain closed until the United States accepted Tehran's demands.
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.
